ledger.x: 19 October 1466: the Second Peace of Thorn creates Royal Prussia.

1569: the Union of Lublin integrates Royal Prussia fully into the Kingdom of Poland: 'Royal Prussia was integrated fully into the Kingdom of Poland' and its parliament 'was reduced to the status of a provincial assembly'; no border changes.

July 1626: after landing at Pillau on 6 July 1626 the Swedes 'rapidly occupied Braniewo, Frombork, Elbląg, Orneta, and Malbork', then 'crossed the Vistula and took Tczew, Gniew, Oliwa and Puck'; Danzig held out.
July 1626: the Swedes occupy Elbląg (Elbing), the town they keep until 1635.
Truce of Altmark: 'In Royal Prussia, Sweden retained the towns of Braunsberg, Frauenberg, and Elbing', so Marienburg, Dirschau, Mewe and Putzig return to Poland.

12 September 1635: the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf: 'the Swedes had to return the territories they occupied in Baltic Prussia' (Elbing, Memel, Pillau; the last two to the Elector of Brandenburg) and withdraw their garrisons.

1637: 'After Duke Bogislaw XIV died childless, the land again became a terra of the Polish Crown' (Lauenburg and Bütow Land page); the Pomeranian Voivodeship page has Bytów, Lębork and Łeba in the voivodeship 'from 1637 to 1657', the Land page from 1641.
Nov-Dec 1655: the Swedes take Toruń in their sweep of Royal Prussia; it 'was besieged from July 1, 1658' and capitulated on 30 December 1658.
Nov-Dec 1655: Graudenz (Grudziądz) taken in the sweep; captured by the Poles in August 1659.
Nov-Dec 1655: Brodnica taken in the sweep; its 'starving garrison surrendered in 1659'.
The Deluge page: 'The Swedes took nearly all of Royal Prussia in Nov-Dec 1655, excluding Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork'; Elbląg is among the towns taken.
Malbork 'not taken in the 1655 sweep', but listed as Swedish in autumn 1657 (siege continued in 1659); the date it fell is not on the page, so 1657 is the first listing.

1657: 'The Treaty of Bydgoszcz, which amended the Treaty of Wehlau, granted it as a fief to the Hohenzollerns of Brandenburg-Prussia, on the terms the Griffins had enjoyed, in return for help against Sweden.'
30 December 1658: Toruń capitulated after a siege from 1 July 1658.
1659: the starving Swedish garrison of Brodnica surrendered (month not on the page).
August 1659: Graudenz captured by the Poles.
3 May 1660: the Treaty of Oliva ends the war.
3 May 1660: the Treaty of Oliva ends the war ('cost Poland most of Livonia'); the page names no change in Royal Prussia.
1772: the First Partition.
1772: Danzig and Thorn, left out of the partition ('Prussia did not take these cities'), stay with the Commonwealth; the Royal Prussia page has the rest of 'the former territory' annexed in 1793.
1 July 1772: Royal Prussia ends as a Polish province; West Prussia succeeds it in the infobox.

wars.name: Thirteen Years' War
wars.outcome: Ended by the Second Peace of Thorn on 19 October 1466: the western half of the Order's state, with Pomerelia, the Chełmno Land, Elbing and Marienburg, goes to Poland; the east remains the Order's fief of the Polish Crown.

wars.name: Polish-Swedish War (1626-1629)
wars.outcome: Gustavus Adolphus landed at Pillau on 6 July 1626; the Truce of Altmark (September 1629) left Sweden Braunsberg, Frauenberg and Elbing in Royal Prussia until the Treaty of Stuhmsdorf (12 September 1635).

wars.name: The Deluge (Second Northern War in Poland)
wars.outcome: The Swedes took nearly all of Royal Prussia in Nov-Dec 1655 except Gdańsk, Puck and Malbork; Toruń fell back to the Poles on 30 December 1658, Graudenz in August 1659; the Treaty of Oliva of 3 May 1660 ended the war.

wars.name: First Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: Prussia took most of Royal Prussia, with Warmia, the Netze District and northern Kuyavia, not Danzig and Thorn.
